groups.title: ListObjects (v1) `Prefix` echo: botocore does not URL-decode it, the test expects it decoded
groups.why: botocore adds `encoding-type=url` to every ListObjects call and decodes the response in `decode_list_object`, whose top-level keys are `Delimiter`, `Marker`, `NextMarker` but not `Prefix` (the v2 and versions decoders do include it; botocore 1.43.123 `handlers.py`). The ListObjects reference lists `Prefix` among the elements returned encoded, and fakes3 encodes it once (`<Prefix>%0A</Prefix>`), so `response['Prefix']` is `%0A` for any server that follows the documentation. Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: SSE-C: CompleteMultipartUpload without the customer key succeeds, the test expects 400
groups.why: After the UploadPart check (fixed: a part with another key is now 400 `InvalidRequest`) the three `test_copy_part_enc[…-sse-c-…]` cases still stop at their last step: `CompleteMultipartUpload` on an SSE-C upload without `x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-*` headers must fail with 400. The CompleteMultipartUpload reference says those headers are 'required only when the object was created using a checksum algorithm', and fakes3 (like S3 today) gives every object one by default, but whether S3 refuses the call when an SDK leaves them out is unconfirmed, and enforcing it would break clients that do not repeat the key on Complete. Not changed.

groups.title: CORS: the test expects a non-preflight request to be matched on `Access-Control-Request-Method` (RGW)
groups.why: Wildcard origins (`*suffix`, `start*end`, `prefix*`) match; the failing step is a `PUT` that carries `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method: GET` and expects the rule that allows `GET` to answer it. AWS evaluates an actual request with its own method and uses the `Access-Control-Request-Method` header only for a preflight `OPTIONS` ('How does Amazon S3 evaluate the CORS configuration'), so the PUT is not matched by the GET-only rule.

groups.title: GET of a key with C1 control characters (valid UTF-8) returns 404, the test expects 400
groups.why: `Key='\xae\x8a-'` is sent as the valid UTF-8 `%C2%AE%C2%8A-`; the test (`fails_on_rgw`, so AWS-valid) wants 400 `Couldn't parse the specified URI.` A key that is not UTF-8 after percent-decoding (`%AE%8A-`) already gets exactly that from s3s (400 `InvalidURI`), so only the C1-control case is open and the rule AWS applies is not documented. Not changed.

groups.title: HEAD of a deleted key in an unversioned bucket expected to carry `x-amz-delete-marker: false`
groups.why: The HeadObject / GetObject reference says of `x-amz-delete-marker`: 'Specifies whether the object retrieved was (true) or was not (false) a Delete Marker. If false, this response header does not appear in the response.' fakes3 sends it only for delete markers, as documented; MinIO and LocalStack fail the same way.

groups.title: PutBucketLogging / bucket logging (NotImplemented)
groups.why: `PutBucketLogging is not implemented yet` (501). 5 AWS-applicable tests here; a further 31+ `bucket_logging` tests are marked `fails_on_aws` (they test RGW's journal/flush extension) and fail the same way.

groups.title: ListBuckets pagination: the test assumes an account without other buckets
groups.why: `list_buckets(MaxBuckets=1)` is paged as AWS documents (`max-buckets`, `continuation-token`, `prefix`, `bucket-region`), but the test asserts that the first page is empty, i.e. that the account owns no bucket. The suite's naming tests leave buckets such as `foo-.bar` behind (their names do not carry the test prefix, so the cleanup skips them), so it cannot pass on a shared server run.

groups.title: Test mutates a header that boto3 re-signs afterwards (the request is valid)
groups.why: The tests add/remove `Authorization`, `Content-Length` or `x-amz-date` in a `before-call` hook, but botocore's signer rewrites those after the hook (checked with boto3 1.43.123 against a stub server: `Authorization` is replaced, `Content-Length` restored, `Date` re-added). The server correctly accepts the valid request, so `ClientError not raised`. They also fail on MinIO and LocalStack. Most are `fails_on_rgw` with a TODO saying so. `test_bucket_create_bad_authorization_invalid_aws2` and `test_bucket_create_bad_date_none_aws2` looked like SigV2 bucket-resource failures until fakes3 worked around that (docs/s3s-workarounds.md): the signed request is then valid and accepted (`Authorization` is rewritten by the signer, there is no `x-amz-date` to remove), so `ClientError not raised`.

groups.title: `check_grants` sorts grants by a key that is None for group grantees (Python 3 TypeError)
groups.why: `got.sort(key=lambda x: x['Grantee'].get('DisplayName'))` runs whenever the first grant has a DisplayName; a group grant (AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers) has none, so Python 3 raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'`. fakes3 lists the owner first, like AWS; MinIO and LocalStack fail identically.

groups.title: SSE-KMS tests expect the key id echoed verbatim; AWS (and fakes3) return the key ARN
groups.why: `assert 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:000000000000:key/testkey-1' == 'testkey-1'` for `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`. AWS always returns the full key ARN; RGW echoes what was sent. The `test_copy_enc` / `test_copy_part_enc` cases with an SSE-KMS destination fail on the same comparison (`assert False` inside the `assert` lambda). Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: GetObject `?partNumber` out of range: test expects 400 InvalidPart (RGW), AWS answers 416 InvalidPartNumber
groups.why: `assert 416 == 400` (and `'InvalidRequest' == 'InvalidPart'` for the SSE-C variant). fakes3 follows the S3 API reference (416). Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: SSE-C read with the wrong key: test expects 400, AWS answers 403
groups.why: `assert 403 == 400` for GET with a well-formed but different customer key; S3 reports 403 `AccessDenied` for a key that does not match the stored MD5 (400 is for malformed/missing headers). Fails on MinIO too.

groups.title: GetBucketEncryption / DeleteBucketEncryption on a fresh bucket expect NotFound; AWS has had SSE-S3 default encryption on every bucket since January 2023
groups.why: `assert '' == 'ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError'`: fakes3 (like current AWS) reports the default AES256 configuration instead of an error. Fails on MinIO too.

groups.title: Re-creating an owned bucket expected to fail with BucketAlreadyExists (RGW)
groups.why: Same call as the CreateBucket group above but the test insists on 409 `BucketAlreadyExists`; on AWS us-east-1 this is a 200. The two groups cannot both pass.

groups.title: PutObject `If-None-Match: <etag>` expected to give 412 (RGW extension; AWS accepts only `*`)
groups.why: Each test passes the `*` cases and then sends `IfNoneMatch=<etag>` expecting 412. The S3 API reference documents only `If-None-Match: *` for PutObject / CompleteMultipartUpload. MinIO passes (it implements the extension); LocalStack fails.

groups.title: Second CompleteMultipartUpload on a finished upload expected to succeed (RGW `check_previously_completed`)
groups.why: `NoSuchUpload` on the repeated complete (the tests comment it as an 'extra' complete); `test_multipart_resend_first_finishes_last` lists PartNumber 1 twice in the complete request and gets `InvalidPart`. All fail on MinIO and LocalStack.

groups.title: Presigned URL with negative / over-long X-Amz-Expires: test expects 403, S3 answers 400
groups.why: `assert 400 == 403`. S3 rejects out-of-range `X-Amz-Expires` with 400 `AuthorizationQueryParametersError`; the test encodes RGW's 403.

groups.title: SSE-KMS without a key id expected to fail; AWS falls back to the managed `aws/s3` key
groups.why: `ClientError not raised` for `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` alone. MinIO and LocalStack reject it, AWS accepts it.

groups.title: Test expects a bucket policy with only an Allow to deny the owner
groups.why: Referer-conditioned `Allow` policy; the test then expects the bucket owner's own GET to be 403. An Allow can never remove the owner's access, so only RGW's policy engine behaves like that (`fails_on_rgw` TODO says it is being fixed).

groups.title: Non-ASCII user metadata expected to round-trip verbatim; AWS returns RFC 2047 `=?UTF-8?B?…?=`
groups.why: `'=?UTF-8?B?SGVsbG8gV29ybGTDqQ==?=' == 'Hello World\xe9'`. fakes3 deliberately encodes like AWS (via `s3s-rfc2047`); boto3 does not decode.

groups.title: Needs RGW's accelerated lifecycle clock (`rgw_lc_debug_interval`)
groups.why: The test waits `lc_debug_interval` seconds for 'one day' to pass; AWS and fakes3 count real days (fakes3 has a virtual clock, but s3-tests cannot drive it).

groups.title: Bucket policy used by the test has no `Resource` (invalid on AWS too)
groups.why: `MalformedPolicy: Syntax errors in policy` for a statement with only Principal/Action; AWS rejects it as well. The test relies on RGW.

groups.title: POST policy uploads: lenient expiration parsing, `tagging` form field ignored, `x-amz-checksum-*` fields refused (s3s)
groups.why: All three live in s3s before fakes3 sees the request. `PostPolicy::from_json` parses `expiration` with the `time` crate's RFC 3339 parser, which accepts the space-separated `2026-10-31 12:00:00+00:00` the test sends (AWS: 400 for an expiration that is not ISO 8601). `PutObject::deserialize_http_multipart` reads the tagging form field as `x-amz-tagging` only, while the POST Object reference documents `tagging` (XML). `validate_conditions_only` refuses any form field without a policy condition (`x-amz-checksum-sha256` is not exempt), so a documented checksum field gives 403. The fourth POST test of the old group, the redirect `Location` with the quoted ETag (`etag=%22…%22`), is fixed in fakes3.

groups.title: S3 Select with JSON output: the tests int() the whole result, AWS answers `{"_1":N}`
groups.why: `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '{"_1":1}'`. `run_s3select_json` asks for JSON output and the tests parse the result as a bare number, which is what Ceph's engine writes for an aggregate; AWS writes one JSON object per record keyed `_1`, `_2`, …, which is what fakes3 returns. The queries themselves run (`count(0) from s3object[*].root`, `min(_1.c1)`).

groups.title: S3 Select: the CSV test expects an empty field to be written as `null`
groups.why: `assert '' != ''` for `select _1 from s3object` on a row that starts with an empty field. Ceph's engine writes NULL as `null`; AWS reads an empty CSV field as an empty string and writes it back as an empty field (a NULL in CSV output is empty too), which is what fakes3 does. The test passed before only because SelectObjectContent answered NotImplemented, a non-empty string.

groups.title: S3 Select: the test looks for Ceph's own error text (`ProcessingTimeError`, `multiple definition of column`)
groups.why: `assert -1 >= 0` on `find('alias {c11} or column not exist in schema')`: the test searches the error for Ceph's wording and code. fakes3 answers a column that the header lacks with 400 `MissingHeaders`, the S3 code for it.

groups.title: RGW tenant syntax in bucket names (`:bucket`, `tenant:bucket`) is not S3
groups.why: The tests address another tenant's bucket as `tenant:bucket` / `:bucket`, which RGW resolves and S3 rejects as `InvalidBucketName`. The `tenant` user is an ordinary second account on fakes3 (the tests that only use its client pass); there is no tenant namespace to map this to.

groups.title: Test reads the bucket owner from `Grants[2]` of a public-read-write ACL (RGW's grant order)
groups.why: `bucket_acl_response['Grants'][2]['Grantee']['ID']` after `create_bucket(ACL='public-read-write')`: RGW lists the owner third, S3 (and fakes3) list the owner first, then `AllUsers` READ and WRITE, so index 2 is a group grantee without `ID` (`KeyError: 'ID'`). The behaviour the tests are about (`bucket-owner-read` / `bucket-owner-full-control` give the bucket owner a grant on the uploader's object) is covered by fakes3's own tests (`tests/multi_user.rs`).

groups.title: Bucket policy with an object action on a bucket ARN is accepted by RGW, rejected by S3
groups.why: `Allow s3:PutObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::bucket` (no `/*`): S3 answers 400 `MalformedPolicy: Action does not apply to any resource(s) in statement` at PutBucketPolicy, which is what fakes3 does; the test expects the policy to be stored.

groups.title: Test adds the `x-amz-tagging` header to the main client but sends the request with the alt client
groups.why: `client.meta.events.register('before-call.s3.PutObject', ...)` is registered on `client`, then `alt_client.put_object(...)` is called, so the request carries no tag and the `s3:RequestObjectTag/security` Allow cannot match: 403 on S3 as well (the test is `fails_on_rgw` with a TODO about it).

out_of_scope.why: Other AWS services, not S3: IAM, STS and SNS need their own endpoints and a multi-account setup; S3 Control is served from a different endpoint. run.sh does not run them (set S3T_ALL=1 to run everything).
